chapter_note: This chapter contains a short cosmological teaching on the unity of the Light versus the self-division of Darkness, then pivots into direct exhortation to the community. The shift to second-person address (“you yourselves…”) marks the pastoral/application layer. The opening attribution to “the enlightener” is a later frame wrapper over an older, impersonal teaching claim.

paragraphs.core_text: [Now as to what affects the] light, behold, at the beginning the Darkness was strong against it; [ ... ] no disunity [ ... ] exists in the light.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue/frame attribution: “Once again the enlightener speaks to his disciples:” (hagiographic compilation frame).
paragraphs.temporal_note: Mixed because a formulaic hagiographic opener (“Once again…”) wraps a cosmological claim about Light/Darkness unity and conflict that reads like older teaching.

paragraphs.core_text: [ ... ] how far [ ... the lig]ht that came forth from [ ... ] in that place in a [ ... ] alone [ ... ] ⟨p.128⟩ the greatness of the light with one another for ever, and nor did one of them transgress the command and order that his brother had entrusted to him forever.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Impersonal, descriptive cosmological-ethical mechanics (perpetual concord, non-transgression of an internal ‘command and order’) without audience address or institutional identification; stays within the cosmic system.

paragraphs.core_text: However, the Darkness, the enemy, was doomed and overcome; because of the arising of disharmony it was divided within itself. Even the kingdom was divided within itself; [and] ev[en] the [powers, who had] left their abyss behind and come up fo[llow-ing] it, were doomed because of the disunity that was present in all of them. The Darkness was destroyed, and its other powers were humiliated,
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the concluding comparison: “because the p[ower] of that first light functions in the same way as the kingdom of this world.” This steps outside the closed cosmological description into an illustrative analogy anchored in ‘this world.’
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core cosmological account of Darkness’s defeat through internal division, then a likely later explanatory analogy to worldly kingdoms (cosmos → ‘this world’), creating a boundary within the paragraph.

paragraphs.core_text: As long as its [associates in the m]ystery are in agreement with it, th[at] kingdom [ ... ] and they marvel at it and it receives glory, the one that [ ... ] and it surpasses and is even more exalted than this other kingdom, which is about [to burst out] against [it].
paragraphs.temporal_note: Continues the impersonal ‘how victory works’ logic (agreement → glory/exaltation over the opposing kingdom) without second-person exhortation. ‘Associates in the mystery’ is ambiguous but can still read as intra-cosmic solidarity.

paragraphs.core_text: Still, the kingdom, [the one that] its associates in the mystery [are in agreement] upon, is compelled to condemn that (other) kingdom; and the[y] are humiliated and come under the hand of this kingdom that is set up against it.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Impersonal continuation of the same cosmological mechanism (united kingdom condemns and subjugates the opposing kingdom). No explicit church/institutional referent appears here.

Direct second-person application (“you yourselves… from your least to your greatest”) and exhortation using the teaching to motivate group harmony; this is institutional/pastoral use of the cosmological motif. (‘Sin’ appears as an opposing power, but the paragraph’s function is exhortation.)

Continues second-person warning and consequence language (“you will be condemned… humiliated under the hand of sin”), characteristic of application voice rather than impersonal cosmological exposition.
Imperative exhortation (“Neither be divided… and you will conquer…”)—pure application voice directed to the community, not a closed-system cosmological mapping.
